items.note: Native converged lighting and shadows remain coherent on ribbons and flat glyphs. The public Python three-guide close-up shows source-anchored triangles and their shadows. No claim of superior presentation quality.

Reviewed 768 and 384 converged and interactive outputs are populated, finite and have no visible missing faces. Native live-backbone GPU regression passed; full orbit/video certification remains outside this still review.

Shared fitted camera; chromatic silhouette width is 357 native versus 354 Mol* pixels (0.85%), recorded in target/cartoon-wedges-gallery/framing.json. Source counts agree: 4779 atoms and 801 residues.

One flat forward triangle per selected source guide, including terminal guides, is demonstrated by geometry tests and the public Python three-guide detail. The view from positive Y mirrors source +X to screen-left: all three tips correctly point left. Glyph dimensions are half the authored cartoon width; source guide identity is retained. Mol* direction visualization establishes the same source traversal, while its thicker prism and theme-relative dimensions are not copied.

reference_notes: Mol* local primary source polymer-direction-wedge.ts was inspected. MolGFX follows the required flat triangle, not the upstream thick prism.
PyMOL 3.1 lacks native per-guide direction wedges; both adapters record an explicit omission.
The first direct reference request retained the unfitted catalog camera and is preserved under reference-unfitted-diagnostic. Only the subsequent harness-fitted request is used for review.
